properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 7:28AM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog will continue to be a concern for the remainder
of the morning. Expect variable visibility reductions down to a
quarter of a mile or less.

Those traveling should be prepared for highly variable road
conditions, including sharp visibility reductions across short
distances. Also, frost deposition may cause slippery spots on
area roads. Use low beam head lights, slow down and allow extra
time to reach your destination.

NWSheadline: Patchy dense fog developing across portions of Cascade and Meagher counties this morning

properties.areaDesc: Northern Copper Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 25 at 5:13AM AKDT until October 25 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 8
inches, highest amounts from Paxson north.

* WHERE...Northern Copper Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the far northern
Copper River Valley beginning early this morning. The heaviest snow
is expected through 4 PM today before slowly tapering off. The best
chance for accumulating snow will be north of mile post 160 with
the highest snow amounts from Paxson north.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:

properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 25 at 4:41AM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 5
feet above the normal high tide line.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 PM AKDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Sunday to 4 AM AKDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Local government officials have reported minor
flooding is occurring along Council Road east of Nome, causing
road damage beyond mile 8, which has caused the closure of the
road beyond that point. Additionally, minor beach erosion is
occurring. For Nome and Golovin, water levels have recently
peaked and will gradually drop into Sunday. While water levels
remain near their apex at this time, in Nome, this can result
in water approaching low-lying homes in Belmont Subdivision
with standing water expected in the port area. For Golovin,
water may inundate any beach property but the roads, buildings
and residences should not be impacted as the water remains
below the berm. Even though water levels drop somewhat, they
will remain normal through early next week. Localized beach
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 5:14AM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 513 AM MST /613 AM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to continue to fall today. However, downstream
impacts will continue near Birdsprings through the remainder of
the day.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST /6:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels will continue to fall through the day,
falling below action stage later this afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 25 at 3:55AM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 10 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southwest winds will build steadily Sunday
morning, becoming strong and gusty by Sunday afternoon. Winds are
expected to be strongest along the coast, but gusts as high as 55
mph are expected to persist inland up to Bethel. Strongest winds
are expected late Sunday night, and winds will begin to diminish
through Monday morning. However, steady southwesterly flow is
expected to continue into midweek.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.description:

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 3:52AM AKDT until October 26 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 40 mph southwest winds
with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...7 PM Sunday to 7 AM AKDT Monday, highest water levels
expected around midnight Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Kipnuk is expected to see water levels 2.0
to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line. Kwigillingok and
Kongiganak are expected to have water levels of 1.0 to 2.0 ft
above the normal highest tide line. Following this system,
steady southwesterly flow is expected to continue for the
Kuskokwim Delta coastline through Tuesday, which may slow the
ability for flood waters to recede.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Palm Beach County
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 25 at 7:43AM EDT until October 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate coastal flooding around periods of high tide,
reaching major flood stage on Monday and Tuesday. Dangerous surf
is expected, with breaker heights reaching 8 to 10 feet. Life
threatening rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Monday to 8 PM EDT
Tuesday. Coastal Flood Advisories will then be necessary
through much of next week after the peak of King Tides. For the
High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Wednesday. For the High Rip
Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 25 at 7:43AM EDT until October 28 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate coastal flooding around periods of high tide,
reaching major flood stage on Monday and Tuesday. Life
threatening rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Monday to 8 PM EDT
Tuesday. Coastal Flood Advisories will then be necessary through
much of next week after the peak of King Tides. For the High
Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 2:49AM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Francisco Bay, Monterey
Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
11:07 AM Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
11:39 AM Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft
MLLW) at 01:43 PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up
to 1.0 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 3:43AM EDT until October 28 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and strong longshore currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT Wednesday. For
the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts will continue through at least
mid week, especially around high tide in areas where dunes have
been compromised. NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe
remains closed. The next high tide is around 7 AM today. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 25 at 2:57AM AST until October 27 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coast of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 25 at 2:51AM AST until October 25 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 25 at 2:20AM EDT until October 28 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
7 to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday
night.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 12:36AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 30 to 40
percent range, especially near and north of the Interstate 10 and
12 corridors. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to remain at or
below 10 mph in most areas, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand
across LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now
includes East Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St
Tammany, Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along
with Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless,
outdoor burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and
all local restrictions followed.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Storm In-fa (30W) is beginning to exit the northern Marshall
Islands as it moves northwest, currently passing near Bikini Atoll.
However, hazardous conditions continue across the region, with
scatterometry this morning showing fresh to strong southwest to west
winds across the northernmost islands and atolls of the RMI. Seas
will remain hazardous to small craft across the area through tonight
as In-fa moves away, due to elevated wind waves and west to
southwest swell, and inter-island travel is strongly discouraged.
Locally heavy showers may produce sudden, strong to near-gale
gusts, leading to locally dangerous conditions. These conditions will
diminish over the next few days as In-fa moves farther away.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

NWSheadline: TROPICAL STORM IN-FA MOVING NORTHWEST, PASSING NEAR BIKINI ATOLL... ...LOCALLY HEAVY SHOWERS, SURGING WEST TO SOUTHWEST WINDS AND SWELL EXPECTED FOR THE NORTHERN RMI

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 24 at 3:10PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued Sunday by 6 AM HST or sooner if
necessary.

* WHAT...Flooding likely along the Rio Grande between Monte Vista and
Alamosa.

* WHERE...Southeastern Rio Grande County and West Central Alamosa
County...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Rio Grande and low lying agricultural
areas in Rio Grande and Alamosa counties is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 525 PM MDT, Emergency management reports flooding of low lying
areas along and near the Rio Grande in Rio Grande county and in
Alamosa county upstream of the city of Alamosa.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Rio Grande and West Central
Alamosa Counties between Monte Vista and Alamosa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

emergency management.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:31PM MDT until October 25 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southwestern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 329 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported heavy rain in the
warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing Between 2
and 4 inches of rain have fallen since Thursday morning.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. This could cause additional rises within rivers,
creeks and streams.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, Bayfield, Ignacio, La Plata, Falfa, Oxford, Bondad,
Hesperus, Breen, Vallecito, Mayday, Kline, Marvel, Tiffany,
Allison and Redmesa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 3:28AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.
properties.instruction:
Listen to advice from local officials. Do NOT drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:31AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.2 feet
late tomorrow evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.
